Recorded by the regional assize-clerks inspecting the chalk horse-downs and lock-channels of the Bjoulsae River valley from Evermor to Bhoriane, guarded by the Order of the Wheel. For three seasons the wardens at place.skycraft.roadside_crooked_crown have noted irregular nocturnal traffic along the approach paths. Tally-marks carved into the outer masonry match the tokens used by Winterborn Reach briar-hearts, river-lock saboteurs, and island-crypt undead. Travellers and patrol-captains are advised to verify all seal-rings before granting passage.

notes.title: Cached Dispatch at place.skycraft.roadside_crooked_crown

rumours: Every tide that clears the South Quay in Daggerfall brings another dispute between the harbor factors and the Knights of the Dragon.
Lantern-bearers on the Ilessan ridge swear they still hear mailed hooves along the old bluff road toward Lysandus's Tomb.
Smugglers off Privateer's Hold use shuttered blue lamps to signal the apple-dories slipping past Glenpoint's customs boom.
A notary in the upper ward claims three baronial charters in Tulune were forged with Direnni sealing-wax.
Tin-miners coming down from the Ilessan Hills carry iron charms against the barrow-wights waking in the chalk coombes.
Castle Daggerfall's armourers have doubled their silver-inlay orders since the full-moon sightings near Camlorn.
Fishermen off Betony channel report wreckage bearing neither Breton nor Redguard hull-marks drifting in on the west swell.
The Mages Guild chapterhouse has offered twenty septims for any intact Ayleid keystone recovered from the cape's sea-caves.
legends: Before the first curtain wall of Castle Daggerfall rose, Nedic hill-kings lit beacon-rings across the cape to warn of Direnni longships.
King Lysandus's warhorse is said to have leaped the harbor chain rather than surrender its rider's banner to the usurper's heralds.
Beneath the oldest guild-bridge in Daggerfall lies the foundation stone where eight petty earls swore the First Charter of the Cape.
The Wyrd of Glenumbra once bound a storm-spirit into the headland oak at Glenpoint so no foreign armada could round the point.
When Chrysamere was last borne through the Lion Gate, every forge-fire on Tannery Row burned white until dawn.
Saint Colette's sea-chapel on the bluff was mortared with crushed oyster-shell and blessed rainwater during the Thrassian Plague.
The buried vaults under Privateer's Hold were carved by a disgraced royal seneschal who hid the crown's war-chest in the tide-tubes.
Old sailors toss a copper piece toward Balfiera whenever the Adamantine Tower catches the last red light of sunset.
songs: O hoist the Dragon's pennant high above the whitewashed quay, where six-and-thirty merchantmen ride anchor in the bay!
From Tulune's apple-orchards to the slate of Glenpoint's tower, the bells of Castle Daggerfall proclaim the kingly hour.
Row soft past Privateer's dark cove when fog lies on the sound, or wake the sleeping halberdiers who keep the sunken ground.
Three chalices for Gothryd's hall, three blades for Breton right, and one cold lamp on Lysandus's tomb to watch the winter night.
The tanner's daughter wed a knight with spurs of silver fine, and traded all her oak-bark vats for charters Sealed in wine.
Strike anvil, smith of Ilessan, and temper well the steel—the road to Camlorn asks a blade that will not turn or yield!
Across the bay the red domes gleam on Sentinel's dry shore, where once our grandsires crossed the oars in Betony's old war.
Sleep sound behind the curtain wall while sea-winds shake the slate; the Knights of the Dragon walk the parapet and gate.

rumours: Villagers below Castle Llugwych bolt their shutters before twilight whenever the red coach is seen on the headland road.
In Anticlere's market square, herbalists sell braided garlic and Stendarr-blessed salt to waggoners bound for the northern hills.
Quarriers in Sensal claims they broke into a Direnni gallery where the wall-crystals still hummed with cold magicka.
Outriders of the Flame have set up a lance-post at the crossroads after three tax-couriers vanished near the karst sinkholes.
Fishermen in the sheltered bay coves say the cliff-harpies have grown bold enough to snatch drying cod from the flakes.
An antiquary at the roadside inn is offering good gold for intact heraldic shields from the ruined peel-towers.
Shepherds on the Sensal downs found ancient bronze urns exposed by last week's cloudburst along the chalk gully.
The parish bailiff has doubled the night-watch around the tithe-chapel after grave-soil was found disturbed.
legends: Castle Llugwych was raised on a sea-stack where Direnni star-gazers once charted the constellations reflected in still tide-pools.
The First Baron of Anticlere won his spurs by holding the narrow karst defile single-handed until the Alcaire relief column arrived.
Beneath the Sensal ridge runs a subterranean river where Nedic cave-painters left ochre handprints three thousand years ago.
When the Crimson Ship anchored off Anticlere, the abbey prioress rang the great bronze bell until a gale drove the plague-hulk out to sea.
The Knights of the Owl and the Knights of the Flame once fought a three-day tournament at Anticlere Cross without a single fatal stroke.
In the deepest cellar of Llugwych Keep stands a dry well that echoes with the surf of the Iliac Bay half a league below.
The boundary-menhirs between Anticlere and Glenumbra are inscribed with parallel Ogham and Aldmeris curses against oath-breakers.
Every spring the village children hang wild daffodil wreaths on the Old Mile-Pillar to thank Kynareth for the warm bay rains.
songs: High stands the keep of Anticlere above the limestone bay, where hawks wheel round the turret-slates at breaking of the day!
Walk briskly past dark Llugwych Crag when evening shadows fall, and ask no hospitality within its banquet-hall.
The Sensal downs are white with sheep, the valleys green with corn, and clear the huntsman's bugle sounds across the dewy morn.
A health unto the border-knights who keep the middle way, from Glenumbra's heather-edge down to the sunlit bay!
Split the white stone with iron wedge and lay the course plumb-true—an Anticlere mason builds a wall to last an era through.
When harpies scream along the cliff and fog creeps up thechine, we pile the driftwood on the hearth and broach a cask of wine.
Two leagues to Alcaire's ferry-slip, three leagues to Camlorn road—the carter sings beside his team and shifts his barley-load.
May Stendarr's righteous beacon shine on chapel, croft, and keep, and guard the folk of Anticlere while all the baronies sleep.

rumours: The Knights of the Owl at Dwynnen Keep have closed the upper archive-tower while scholars examine a newly recovered Direnni codex.
Timber-drovers floating spruce rafts down from the Wrothgar foothills report clanless Orc scouts watching the river-bends.
At the Kynareth sea-chapel, coastal pilots leave carved bone ship-models before attempting the northern shoals.
A factor in the port ward is hiring guards to escort a mule-train of salt-herring and linen up the mountain pass.
Old barrows on the Dwynnen headlands have begun glowing with pale wisp-light after the autumn equinox gales.
Smugglers using the sea-caves below the chalk cliffs were driven out last week by a pack of salt-marsh dreugh.
The baronial falconer lost a prized white gyrfalcon toward the northern crags and offers fifty septims for its jesses.
Blacksmiths by the harbour sluice say mountain iron from the border mines has been arriving brittle and cursed.
legends: Dwynnen's sea-wall was laid by Direnni geomancers who sang the granite blocks into interlocking courses that need no mortar.
The Order of the Owl was chartered here to guard the secret libraries left behind when the Elven Hegemony withdrew to Balfiera.
On the highest bluff above the bay stands the Mariner's Cairn, where every lost ship of the northern coast has a named slate.
During the Frost-Year, a white whale beached itself below Dwynnen Chapel and gave oil enough to keep every hearth burning till spring.
Baroness Ysolde the Wise settled a war between three mountain clans by weighing their grievances against bags of salt on the quay scales.
The whispering gallery in Dwynnen Keep carries a spoken word from the harbour water-gate straight to the lord's solar.
Where the cold hill-streams meet the bay, water-nymphs once braided reed-crowns for fishers who threw back the first catch of the tide.
An iron anchor twice the height of a man stands in the market-place, dredged from the wreck of an Atmoran long-keel.
songs: Where northern pines meet bay-side chalk on Dwynnen's windy shore, the Owl-Knights keep their silent watch above the breakers' roar!
Ring out, sea-chapel bell of bronze, across the foaming bar, and guide the herring-luggers home beneath the evening star.
We fell the tall spruce on the crag and raft it down the stream, to lay the keels of Dwynnen port with adze and oakum-seam.
The scholar in the Owl-Tower reads by a whale-oil lamp, while pikemen pace the sea-wall cold and stamp away the damp.
Cast nets into the silver Firth when Kynareth is kind, and leave a tithe upon the rock for those the sea-gods find.
From Wrothgar's snows the cold wind blows across the barony's firth, yet warm the cider-kettle sings beside the tavern hearth.
No corsair dares the northern shoals where Dwynnen's beacons blaze, and every reef is charted down in books of ancient days.
Here's to the Baron's falcon white and to the Owl of Grey, that guard the northern portal of the great Iliac Bay!

rumours: Drovers on the Camlorn turnpike travel in armed threes since the timber-wolves began hunting by daylight.
The Beldama Wyrd sisters have hung woven rowan-wheels on the boundary oaks outside Westtry's barrow-field.
Quarry-wardens in Crosswych Gorge uncovered an iron-grated vault whose seal predates the Camoran Dynasty.
In Daenia's fen-villages, the dyke-reeves burn peat-tar at dusk to keep the marsh-lights from luring cattle into the mire.
A scholar from Camlorn's cathedral close vanished near Cath Bedraud with a satchel of First Era burial rubbings.
The Order of the Lily has posted sentries at the old toll-bridge after blood-cult tokens turned up in the mill-race.
Fishermen at Eagle's Brook say the river runs warm and metallic whenever the forge-fires under the headland ruins are lit.
Merchants in Northmoor pay double guard-hire whenever the sea-haar rolls thick across the standing stones.
legends: At the Great Wyrd Tree, four elemental guardians were bound into the roots when the first Breton druids made peace with the earth-bones.
Cath Bedraud holds the stone biers of thirty petty kings who fell in a single misty afternoon fighting the Empress Hestra's legions.
Camlorn's black-slate cathedral was raised over a sacred well where Mara's handmaidens healed the survivors of the Red Eagle border wars.
The Tomb of Lost Kings was sealed with seven bronze keys, each entrusted to a different hill-monastery across Glenumbra.
When the Bloodthorn cult first tried to corrupt the Wyrd groves, the white harts of the moor trampled their altars into the peat.
Grimley Tor's watch-ring was stacked by giant-kin before the Direnni taught men to square ashlar or raise a pointed arch.
They say the bell in Northmoor's abbey tolls of its own accord whenever a crowned ruler of Camlorn dies.
In Hag Fen, the oldest bog-oaks preserve the shields of an entire knightly company that marched off the causeway in a winter gale.
songs: Through Camlorn's mist the lancets rise in slate of raven-blue, where silver-wrights and choir-boys sing the morning office through.
Step never off the causeway stones when Daenia's fog is deep, for under reed and cotton-grass the ancient barrows sleep.
The Wyrd-maid by the rowan tree has neither coin nor crown, yet dukes take off their steel gauntlets before they sit them down.
At Crosswych where the hammers ring against the split blue stone, every roof in Glenumbra claims a gable of its own.
O hunt no stag in Cath Bedraud when autumn moons are red, lest hounds come back with cold white eyes and answer to the dead!
Give me a coat of Camlorn frieze and stout ash in my hand, to walk the heather ridgeway across the western land.
From Eagle's Brook to Northmoor's cliff the sea-wind salt and keen drives in the herring-busses where the chalk-headlands lean.
Bar fast the oak at nightfall, set rowan by the door, and let the wolves of Glenumbra howl out upon the moor.

rumours: Granary-reeves at Kambria have locked the lower grain-vaults after finding cultist chalk-marks on the tithe-pillars.
At Alcaire Castle, the Knights of the Flame are recruiting experienced delve-guards to clear the coastal sea-caves.
Koeglin shipwrights say the dreugh in the outer sound have been tearing lobster-pots and dragging buoys into the kelp-trenches.
Teamsters at the Weeping Giant way-station report Supernal Dreamers preaching strange omens along the limestone ridge road.
A chest of Direnni astrolabes salvaged off Alcaire Island has set three guild-factors bidding against the court wizard.
Windmillers on the central ridge claim the night-mists carry the smell of brimstone from the old Vaermina fanes.
Toll-wardens at the stone river-bridges are inspecting every covered wain for smuggled Dwemer scrap and unlicensed potions.
Abbey herbalists near Shinji's Scarp have asked travellers to report any blighted lavender or frost-burned orchard trees.
legends: Alcaire Island's cliff-keep still preserves the vaulted chamber where the young Hjalti Early-Beard learned the sword-forms of High Rock.
Shinji's Scarp takes its name from the Honour-Marshal of Orsinium who died holding the breach so both armies' wounded could withdraw.
The Weeping Giant monolith was carved from a single pillar of grey limestone where a First Era truce was sworn in rainwater and wine.
Kambria's double-walled granaries once withstood a two-year siege while the defenders baked bread from fifty-year-old tithe corn.
When the Knights of the Flame were founded, their first grandmaster lit his lance-beacon from a lightning-struck oak on the headland.
Beneath Koeglin's careening beach lie the petrified ribs of an Aldmeri flagship wrecked during the first mapping of the Iliac Bay.
The abbey bells of Stormhaven are cast with ameasure of silver from the Direnni tribute-chests so their peal carries three leagues.
Every milestone along the high turnpike marks a League of the Chantry where pilgrims once rested between Daggerfall and Wayrest.
songs: On Alcaire's cliff the beacon burns above the narrow sound, where once a general's cradle rocked upon the island ground!
Bring wheat to Kambria's stone barn and oak to Koeglin's shore—Stormhaven feeds the western bay and ribs the ships of war.
The Weeping Giant stands in stone beside the turnpike grey, and counts the iron-rimmed waggon-wheels that rumble down the way.
Ride with the Knights of Flame, lads, when autumn gales blow cold, with scarlet surcoats over plate and spurs of burnished gold!
At Shinji's Scarp the heather grows above the broken wall, where Orc and Breton kept their word before the bugle's call.
Turn, windmill, on the limestone ridge and grind the barley fine, while coopers hoop the island casks for Alcaire's amber wine.
Beware the dreugh-lights in the cove when spring-tides flood the weir, and keep your boat within the boom until the dawn is clear.
From Koeglin Quay to Wayrest Gate the flagstones run like thread, binding twenty baronies where merchant wains are led.

rumours: Syndics on the Wayrest canal-locks are hiring private blades after three spice-lighters were boarded in the marsh-fog.
Castle Wayrest's chancery clerks whisper that two merchant-princes have mortgaged their quay-warehouses to pay corsair ransoms.
Under the old guild-arcades, sewer-wardens sealed an iron grate after hearing necromantic chanting beneath the counting-houses.
The Mages Guild customs-inspectors at the Bjoulsae boom seized a crate of soul-gems bearing the mark of the Worm Cult.
At the Chantry of Akatosh, pilgrims say the hourglass altar-lamps flickered blue the night the bay fleet weighed anchor.
Dock-taverns along thefen-wharves are full of sailors swearing a black caravel slipped past the harbour chain without a sound.
Court tailors in the noble ward cannot keep velvet or silver thread in stock ahead of the autumn charter-ball.
Night-watchmen on the bridge-ward carry brass whistles and salt-bags whenever the reed-fog rises out of the estuary.
legends: Wayrest began as a timber trading-stockade on the Bjoulsae mud-flats before the Gardner kings walled the canals in white limestone.
During the Great Sack, the Chantry priests sank the golden dragon-lectern into the deepest lock-pit so the raiders took only brass.
The Harbour Chain of Wayrest was forged in a hundred smithies across High Rock, each link stamped with a guild-house signet.
Queen Barenziah's winter garden in the palace keep was planted with night-blooming Morrowind lilies watered by heated cisterns.
Beneath the Merchant-Princes' Exchange lies the Old Counting-Vault, where First Era tallies are still chiselled into slate slabs.
Saint Pelin's reliquary was carried round the canal-walls three times during the red-mist fever, and the wind turned within the hour.
They say any coin dropped into the Founders' Fountain by the customs quay will return to its owner's purse threefold if the venture is honest.
The seven stone bridges of Wayrest are keyed so that pulling a single master-pin in the keep drops the central spans into the river.
songs: In Wayrest where the Bjoulsae meets the waters of the bay, a hundred silken guild-flags snap above the marble quay!
Count well your septims on the bridge and guard your ledger-book, for Wayrest factors take their tithe by charter, seal, and hook.
The canal-boats glide with lanterns lit beneath the arches low, while viols play in palazzo halls where chandelier-lights glow.
Drop down the iron harbour-chain when corsair topsails gleam, and man the bastion culverins across the estuary stream!
From Evermor the timber rafts come floating down the flood, to build the ships of Wayrest town above the river-mud.
Akatosh keeps the golden glass within the Chantry nave, and measures out the hours of kings, of merchant, and of knave.
Drink red Colovian in the hall and cider on the pier—every tongue in Tamriel buys cargoat Wayrest weir!
Though Daggerfall boasts older blood and Camlorn older stone, the gold of all the Iliac Bay bows down to Wayrest's throne.

rumours: Since the crimson mists gathered round the Doomcrag, patrols from Shornhelm ride only between sunrise and the ninth bell.
In Northpoint's salt-warehouses, captains check every crewman's shadow before signing articles for the northern passage.
Refugees from Hoarfrost Downs say the blood-fiends in the crag-castles answer to a noble house that supposedly died out an era ago.
Magister Corwen in Shornhelm is paying silver for any uncorrupted Ayleid shards brought down from the western tors.
At Ravenwatch Castle, the household guards drink spiced wine mixed with alchemical wards and keep the drawbridge raised at noon.
Sheep-farmers in the chalk hollows have fenced off the old sinkholes where gargoyles roost among the basalt spires.
The Tri-Barony Council in Shornhelm has posted bounties on three necromancers seen robbing the hillside ossuaries.
Whalers out of Dorell's coast-hamlets report ice-floes and ghost-lights drifting south from the Sea of Ghosts.
legends: The Doomcrag was raised by Ayleid sorcerer-kings to house the Lightless Remnant, a shard of star-metal that drank the green from the hills.
Shornhelm took its name when High King Emeric's grandsire clove a rebel earl's visor in two on the steps of the upper keep.
Northpoint's lighthouse was built by House Dorell using black basalt quarried from a meteor-crater on the northern cape.
The Crypt of Exiles beneath the moors holds the embalmed hearts of every Rivenspire baron who died beyond the borders of High Rock.
Count Verandis Ravenwatch swore an ancient compact in the vaults of Lorkrata to police the blood-lines of the northern crags.
When the Ranser's War raged across the pass, a single company of Shornhelm halberdiers held the Dead Wolf Gorge forseven days.
The basalt needles of Westmark Moor are said to be the petrified spears of an army that marched against the Divines in the Dawn.
Every winter solstice, the bells of Shornhelm toll thirteen strokes for the lost village of Moira's Hope.
songs: Black rise the spires of Shornhelm town against the moorland sky, where three proud barons hold the pass and let no traitor by!
Look never toward the Doomcrag's height when red the lightning plays, for broken is the Ayleid ward of old Merethic days.
At Northpoint where the northern sea beats hard upon the stone, the lighthouse-keeper trims his wick and watches all alone.
Bar door and shutter, hill-men all, and hang the iron charm—the hounds of Lorkrata are loose above the moorland farm!
House Dorell rules the sea-girt cape, House Tamrith holds the down, and Montclair's ruined banners rot above the sunken town.
Spare one dry log for Stendarr's fire and one prayer for the dead, who sleep beneath the basalt cairns where heather-roots are spread.
Though Glenumbra has greener fields and Wayrest richer gold, the steel of stony Rivenspire is faithful, keen, and bold!
When morning clears the raven-crags and drives the mist to sea, the bugles on the Shornhelm wall blow out reveille free.

rumours: Lock-keepers along the Bjoulsae have strung iron chains across the weirs after Reachmen coracles were spotted in the mist.
In Evermor's horse-fairs, Bhoriane breeders are asking forty septims extra for destriers trained to stand against briar-heart magic.
The Order of the Wheel has doubled its river-patrols between the chalk bluffs and the border bridge at Bangkorai Garrison.
Barge-captains at the Crooked Tortoise swear the drowned crypts on the river-isles open their bronze doors when the water drops.
Winterborn raiders drove off twenty head of cattle from the eastern downs before the outriders from Farrun could cut them off.
Herbalists in the river-meadows warn that hagraven covens have poisoned the upper boundary-springs with black nightshade.
Quarry-barges carrying limestone down to Wayrest now travel in convoys of four with crossbowmen on the deck-houses.
An old Redguard sword-master at the ford-inn is teaching caravan guards how to break a Reachman shield-rush.
legends: The Horse-Oath of the Bjoulsae was sworn when Breton knights and river-folk poured a helm of river-water over the first boundary stone.
Evermor's citadel was founded at the highest ford where the salt-tide of the Iliac Bay ceases to push back the mountain current.
On the Isle of Crypts in mid-river sleep the river-kings who taxed every log and fleece before Wayrest built its first quay.
When the Red Eagle's host marched west out of the Reach, the Order of the Wheel broke the great dam and swept their vanguard down the gorge.
The White Mare of Bhoriane is carved into the chalk escarpment above the valley; shepherds scour the turf every fifth spring so she gleams.
Farrun's northern bastion was built with mortar mixed with bull's blood and forge-slag to withstand the frost-giants of Wrothgar.
They say a sunken treasure-barge from the Direnni tribute-fleets still lies in the deep eddy below the Three Sisters Weir.
No horse bred on the Bjoulsae downs will ever Drink from a stream where a hag's shadow has fallen.
songs: Flow broad and green, O Bjoulsae stream, between the chalk-bluffs white, where barge-poles flash by day and lanterns drift by night!
The Bhoriane colt has hooves of flint and wind within his chest—no courser in the Western Reach can match himat the test.
Keep watch upon the eastern ford where heather meets the sedge, for Winterborn with bone-tipped spears creep down the canyon's edge!
At Evermor the toll-bell rings above the timber-weir, and every raft from Wrothgar pays its custom at the pier.
Turn, Wheel of Order, on the shield of every river-knight, who guards the lock, the meadow-dyke, and the drover's camp-fire light!
Heave on the tow-rope, barge-lads all, and walk the gravel bank, while heronsfish among the reeds where ancient galleys sank.
From Farrun's windy mountain-gate down to the salt-marsh boom, the valley echoes with the smith, the horse-fair, and the loom.
Raise high the stirrup-cup of mead before we ford the flood—the Bjoulsae keeps its ancient oath in water, stone, and blood!

rumours: In the great foundries of Orsinium, forge-wives are testing a new seam of black orichalcum hauled down from the Frostbreak ridges.
Outriders on the Jehanna road report Vosh Rakh zealots ambushing supply-sledges that refuse to swear the Old Pariah's oath.
At Fharun Stronghold, sea-watches have spotted ice-wolves and frost-trolls driven down to the beaches by a blizzard on the peaks.
Echatere-herders in the high valleys hang iron clappers on their lead-bulls to scare off the harpy flocks nesting in the crags.
Scholars invited into Orsinium's museum are debating whether the lower ruin-vaults belong to the First or Second city of Torug.
Clanless raiders holding the old Dwemer air-shafts have begun firing steam-Crossbows at prospectors along the eastern ridge.
In Jehanna's dockside taverns, Nordic fur-traders and Breton factors argue over whale-bone tariffs until the town watch clears the room.
Wise-women of the mountain clans warn that the Riekr tribes in the ice-caves have found a cache of ancient dwarven fire-salts.
legends: Torug gro-Igron raised the first Orsinium when he bound the wandering mountain clans with the Law of the Forge and the Code of Mauloch.
The Great Brazier of Orsinium is fed with anthracite and mammoth-tallow so its flame never dies through the nine-month mountain winter.
During the Thirty-Year Siege, the Shield-Wife Gaiden Shinji's heirs held the Iron Gate until the stones themselves melted from dragon-fire.
High in the Wrothgarian peaks stands the Frozen Anvil, where Malacath is said to have struck the first vein of orichalcum into the rock.
Fharun's cliff-fortress was carved out of a black basalt headland that resisted three Atmoran landing-fleets in the Merethic Era.
The Dwemer of Rkindaleft built harmonic brass pipes through the glaciers to heat their subterranean gardens with deep magma vents.
When an Orsimer warchief falls in clean battle, his armour is melted down into the hinge-pins of his stronghold's main gate.
The Blood-Price Stone at the crossroads of Wrothgar bears a thousand chisel-notches, each marking a feud settled without wiping out a clan.
songs: Strike, hammer, on the red-hot bar while bellows roar and sigh—Orsinium's iron towers rise against the winter sky!
No mortar binds our granite blocks, no softness dulls our blade; in Wrothgar's frost and furnace-smoke the Orsimer are made.
Drive up the shaggy echatere along the icy trail, where harpies wheel above the pass and mountain blizzards wail!
Remember Gaiden Shinji's word upon the tourney-field: the best technique is lived by those who never drop their shield.
From Fharun's black and foaming cliff to Jehanna's frozen bay, the clan-watch keeps the beacon-fires burning night and day.
Let Breton lords count parchment-scrolls and Redguards boast the sand—the mountain gives its iron ore only to the strong right hand!
Pour out the bitter barley-bree and set the boar-ribs down, for smith and hunter, wife and chief, within the stronghold town.
Though thrice our walls were cast in dust by jealous kings of men, while one forge burns in Wrothgar's hills, Orsinium stands again!
